macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures edge higher as oil retreats after Iran-related tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures rose modestly as oil prices steadied and investors weighed renewed geopolitical risk after fresh U.S. strikes on Iran. Reuters said the move followed a broader rebound in global markets after earlier anxiety about the conflict.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound while investors assess U.S.-Iran conflict risk
items.summary: Reuters reported that futures recovered as oil prices eased, even as traders remained focused on the potential impact of U.S.-Iran tensions on markets and energy prices. The same report noted strong demand for leverage in equity funding markets.

items.title: Fed’s Williams says he does not expect a sustained surge in energy prices
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said he was not looking for a lasting rise in energy prices despite the renewed conflict in the Middle East. The comment helped frame how central bankers are viewing the inflation risk from geopolitical shocks.

items.title: ECB accounts show inflation still seen above target despite expected rate cuts
items.summary: European Central Bank meeting accounts indicated policymakers were presented with projections showing inflation remaining above target into next year despite nearly three expected rate cuts. The release reinforces that the ECB remains focused on persistent price pressures.

items.title: PepsiCo beats second-quarter revenue estimates
items.summary: PepsiCo reported second-quarter revenue above Wall Street expectations, helped by stronger U.S. salty-snack demand and resilient zero-sugar soda sales. Reuters said the results pointed to continued consumer demand in key product categories.

items.title: U.S. housing data weakens as existing home sales unexpectedly fall
items.summary: U.S. existing home sales unexpectedly declined in June as elevated mortgage rates and record house prices kept buyers on the sidelines. The data adds to signs of a slower housing market even as the broader labor market remains stable.

items.title: Weekly jobless claims fall, reinforcing labor-market stability
items.summary: U.S. weekly jobless claims dropped, supporting the view that the labor market remains in a 'slow-hire, slow-fire' pattern. Reuters said the data came despite a sharp slowdown in payroll growth in June.

items.title: Reuters: corporate earnings optimism keeps supporting the U.S. stock rally
items.summary: Reuters reported that rising optimism over corporate earnings has helped drive U.S. stocks to new highs in 2026, even as analysts warn that stronger profit growth is now a higher bar for the market. The piece highlights the market’s dependence on continued earnings momentum.

items.title: SK Hynix U.S. share offering reportedly more than seven times oversubscribed
items.summary: A Reuters report said demand for SK Hynix’s U.S. share offering was more than seven times the shares available. That level of demand signals strong investor appetite for the chipmaker’s equity story.

items.title: MarketScreener: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures tick higher as tech stabilizes
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were up as technology shares steadied. The same feed showed notable 24-hour moves including the S&P 500 down 1.44% and the Nasdaq 100 down 3.29%.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rises above $63K as risk appetite improves
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed above $63,000 amid easing oil prices and a broader shift toward risk assets. Market coverage also noted ongoing volatility and recent liquidation pressure across crypto markets.

items.title: Bitcoin whales push BTC toward $64K as Coinbase Premium breaks key level
items.summary: On-chain data suggests large Bitcoin holders helped lift BTC toward $64,000 while the Coinbase Premium indicator turned supportive. The move points to renewed U.S.-led spot demand.

items.title: Strategy sells 3,588 BTC, putting corporate Bitcoin selling in focus
items.summary: Strategy’s sale of 3,588 Bitcoin has drawn market attention because it raises questions about whether more corporate holders could sell into weakness. Analysts are watching the move for its effect on sentiment and liquidity.

items.title: Sen. Wyden urges Senate leaders to preserve blockchain developer protections
items.summary: Sen. Ron Wyden is pressing Senate leaders to keep contested protections for blockchain developers in a broader crypto bill. The dispute centers on how much legal clarity developers should receive under federal policy.

items.title: European Commission reportedly looks to expand MiCA coverage
items.summary: A report says the European Commission is considering broadening MiCA to cover tokenization and non-EU stablecoin issuers. That would extend Europe’s crypto rulebook beyond its current scope.

items.title: Hong Kong SFC forces crypto platforms to ditch SMS authentication
items.summary: Hong Kong’s securities regulator is pushing crypto platforms away from SMS-based authentication to stronger security standards. The move reflects tighter operational scrutiny on exchanges and custodians.

items.title: Ripple wins MiCA CASP authorization in Luxembourg
items.summary: Ripple secured MiCA authorization from Luxembourg’s CSSF, allowing it to offer regulated crypto payments across 30 EEA countries. The approval expands Ripple’s global regulatory footprint and supports its European payments strategy.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin outlines a multi-year 'Lean Ethereum' rebuild
items.summary: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin described a 3-to-4-year protocol overhaul focused on quantum safety, privacy, cheaper data storage, and possibly replacing the EVM. The proposal signals a major long-term technical roadmap for Ethereum.

items.title: Solana activates its first formal on-chain governance system
items.summary: Solana launched its first formal on-chain governance system, giving large validators proposal rights and delegators override voting power. The change marks a significant step in how the network will make protocol decisions.

items.title: Binance Wallet adds Plume yield vault access to institutional funds
items.summary: Binance Wallet integrated Plume’s yield vault offering, which provides access to funds from Invesco and Bitwise. The development expands crypto wallet-based access to tokenized or yield-bearing financial products.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta plans to start manufacturing its own AI chip
items.summary: Reuters reports that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September, part of a broader effort to boost computing power to 14 gigawatts next year. The move signals continued industry investment in custom AI infrastructure and tighter control over hardware supply.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: Reuters says xAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model so far and targeting coding and agentic workflows. The release adds to the intensifying competition among frontier model makers on software engineering and autonomous task performance.

items.title: OpenAI copyright dispute escalates with new sanctions motion
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that news publishers have accused OpenAI of hiding tools and datasets that could identify copyrighted journalism in ChatGPT outputs, escalating the ongoing lawsuit. The new motion for sanctions highlights continued legal pressure around training data and output provenance.

items.title: UN digital agency launches initiative to improve trust in AI agents
items.summary: Reuters reports that the United Nations' digital technology agency announced a new initiative aimed at improving trust in AI agents. The effort reflects growing concern about accountability, oversight, and safety as AI systems become more autonomous.

items.title: Humain and Cohere team up on AI compute and sovereign models
items.summary: Reuters reports that Saudi Arabia-backed Humain and Canadian AI firm Cohere will collaborate on AI compute and sovereign AI model development. The partnership underscores the rising global competition for compute capacity and regionally controlled AI infrastructure.

items.title: Google will now disclose which ads are made with AI
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Google is changing its ad transparency practices to disclose which advertisements are created with AI. The move suggests growing pressure on major platforms to label synthetic content and improve transparency in digital advertising.

items.title: Paris-based voice startup Gradium raises $100 million seed round
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Gradium, a Paris-based AI voice startup, raised a $100 million seed round with backing from Nvidia. The large early-stage financing signals strong investor interest in voice AI and foundation-model-adjacent infrastructure.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India removes import duties on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on several parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, cutting 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could lower input costs for manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple and Broadcom expand chip-supply deal in multibillion-dollar agreement
items.summary: Apple said it plans to spend more than $30 billion under a chip-supply agreement reached with Broadcom, which will also expand a factory in Colorado. The deal strengthens Apple’s domestic chip supply chain.

items.title: EU lawmakers back temporary rules for platforms to remove child sexual abuse material
items.summary: EU lawmakers backed reinstating interim rules that would let Google, Meta, and other platforms detect and remove online child sexual abuse material. The proposal is intended to avoid a gap in enforcement while longer-term rules are negotiated.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: Meta is preparing to start manufacturing an AI chip from September as part of a broader effort to expand computing capacity. An internal memo reviewed by Reuters said the company aims to boost total computing power to 14 gigawatts next year.

items.title: Amazon, Google, and Microsoft-backed cloud and data-center spending continues to accelerate
items.summary: Industry reporting highlighted continued large-scale spending on chips and infrastructure tied to data-center expansion, including a major Micron factory expansion in Hiroshima. The investment wave underscores ongoing demand for compute capacity across the tech sector.

items.title: Bending Spoons completes Nasdaq IPO after years of acquisitions
items.summary: Bending Spoons’ Nasdaq listing capped more than a decade of acquisitions that transformed the Italian company into a highly leveraged internet business. The deal marks one of the more significant consumer-tech market debuts recently.

items.title: European startup funding rebounds strongly in Q2
items.summary: European startups raised $24 billion in Q2, up 66% year over year and the strongest quarter in four years. The UK led regional funding with $10.4 billion, ahead of Germany and France.

items.title: Apple supplier Luxshare falls in Hong Kong trading debut
items.summary: Luxshare, a key Apple supplier, slipped 1.6% on its Hong Kong market debut after raising about $3.1 billion. It was the city’s biggest listing so far in 2026.
